issue: `has_invalid_unicode_scalar` never stops on cyclic input. It keeps no record of containers it has already visited, so a payload like `d = {"self": d}` loops forever and its pending list grows without limit. I checked this: `Observation(payload=d)` was still running after 3 s. Before this change the recursive copier raised `RecursionError`, and `RawFirstDecoder` turned that into a `raw.unknown` gap. Now a driver bug that builds a cyclic payload freezes the supervisor's decode path, along with the timeout and cleanup steps that wait on it. Both design reviewers raised this as a non-blocker. Fix: track the `id()` of containers already visited, either skipping them or raising `ValueError`. That is about 3 lines and keeps the scan iterative
reason: Settled limitation: the reviewed helper contract is explicitly acyclic JSON-like containers; native json.loads cannot create cycles. Preserve the witnessed hang; no cycle-guard scope expansion.

issue: The R2 class of bug still exists at display time, outside this PRD's scope. `bounded_detail` strips only C0 controls and 7-bit CSI. The TUI's `display_text` drops all Cc/Cf/Cs/Zl/Zp characters (src/ovcaq/tui/model.py:57). Confirmed: `"lane sk-abc\u200b<36 chars>"` (also with \x85, \x9b, \u00ad, \u2060 instead of \u200b) passes redaction unchanged and the TUI shows the joined `sk-abcabcdef…` token. Activity text and tool details (src/ovcaq/drivers/codex_events.py:32, src/ovcaq/drivers/codex_events.py:127) strip nothing, so a NUL-split token also renders whole on screen. This needs a durable home (a PRD or issue)

issue: The supervisor's catch-all handler builds `SessionSummary(..., str(error), ...)`. If the error text carries surrogateescape bytes (a non-UTF-8 path), the new `SessionSummary` check raises `ValueError` inside the handler and `_conclude` is skipped, so the failure record is lost. Not a regression: the strict encode in src/ovcaq/runtime/_session_io.py:19 already failed on such text
reason: Pre-existing arbitrary exception/path surrogate handling; retain for later scoped runtime failure work.

issue: The pre-decode check assumes every driver parses frames with plain `json.loads`. A plugin driver that unwraps a prefix or applies its own escapes skips the pre-mutation check. The model still rejects the bad strings, so nothing crashes, but such a driver can change its state before the `Observation` constructor raises. Every frame (up to 1 MiB) is also parsed twice; the PRD sets no performance limit
reason: Prefix-unwrapping/custom-escape plugin drivers are outside this native JSON frame contract. Preserve malformed/non-JSON delegation; no generic rollback framework.

issue: The review-1 two-pass `bounded_detail` leaks the tail of a split token. When the control sits after 20 or more body characters, pass 1 redacts the head. Control removal then glues the tail onto `[REDACTED]`, and pass 2 finds no `sk-` or `Bearer` prefix to match. I ran it to confirm: `bounded_detail('Diagnostic sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\x1b[0m0123456789ABCDEF')` returns `'Diagnostic [REDACTED]0123456789ABCDEF'`, the real `turn.failed` payload detail is the same, and `'Bearer '+'a'*23+'\x00bbbbbbbb'` returns `'Bearer [REDACTED]bbbbbbbb'`. Task 3's strip-first order redacted these fully, and pre-PRD code leaked the same way. This breaks two PRD rules ("ANSI/NUL splits of ordinary synthetic tokens are redacted", "synthetic credential fragments never enter normalized details") and makes docs/driver-protocol.md:224 claim too much. Every split test cuts at `token[:6]`, so no test catches it. Fix: before control removal, absorb token characters stuck to a marker across recognized controls with `re.sub(rf"\[REDACTED\](?:{controls})+[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "[REDACTED]", sanitize_text(protected))`. I probed this on both leaks plus `x\x00sk-…`, the OSC case and the cap reproducer, and all came out fully redacted (I did not run the suite with it). Also add SPLIT_DETAILS cases that split after 20 or more body characters, for both bare and Bearer tokens
